kept.title: Unsafe execution of user-controlled file paths
kept.description: The benchmark suite in benchmark/index.js executes JavaScript files from the directory using child_process.spawn. If an attacker can place a malicious file in the directory, it will be executed with the same privileges as the process.
steps_to_exploit: Place a file named `malicious.js` in the benchmark directory.
Run `npm run bench`.
The malicious code executes via child_process.spawn.
kept.impact: Remote code execution within the environment running the benchmark scripts.

kept.title: Disabling TLS strict-ssl for legacy environments
kept.description: The CI workflow forces strict-ssl to false for Node.js 0.10 environments, exposing the build pipeline to man-in-the-middle attacks when fetching dependencies.
steps_to_exploit: Intercept network traffic during the CI pipeline for a Node 0.10 job.
Inject malicious content into the downloaded NPM package.
The build process accepts the tampered package.
kept.impact: Compromise of the build pipeline and potential inclusion of malicious code in the distribution.

kept.title: Insecure reliance on potentially spoofed header
kept.description: The `proxy-addr` module is fundamentally designed to trust header information (`x-forwarded-for`). If `trust` is misconfigured or a proxy is misconfigured, an attacker can spoof their IP address.
steps_to_exploit: Identify an application that trusts the proxy-addr output.
Inject a fake `X-Forwarded-For` header in the HTTP request.
The application logic uses the forged IP for security decisions (e.g., rate limiting, access control).
kept.impact: Security bypasses, including circumventing IP-based firewalls or access controls.

kept.title: Unauthenticated access to sensitive system information
kept.description: The benchmark files print local paths and command arguments to the console, potentially leaking environment details or internal directory structures.
steps_to_exploit: Execute `npm run bench`.
Observe output containing local file paths and internal execution details.
kept.impact: Information disclosure of the internal build environment structure.

kept.title: Improper input validation in IP subnet range parsing
kept.description: The logic in `parseipNotation` allows wide ranges or invalid netmasks that could result in unexpected trust behavior.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a malformed CIDR notation (e.g., with non-numeric masks) to the `compile` function.
Observe if the code allows unexpected IP ranges into the 'trusted' list.
kept.impact: Security misconfiguration leading to unintended network access.

kept.title: Use of deprecated and vulnerable CI configuration
kept.description: The CI workflow tests against EOL (End-of-Life) Node.js versions (0.10, 0.12, io.js, etc.) which have multiple unpatched vulnerabilities and lack modern security features.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger the CI workflow.
Dependencies may be installed in insecure environments that lack security patches or proper sandbox isolation.
kept.impact: Insecure testing environments leading to unreliable security verification.

kept.title: Insecure installation of global NPM packages
kept.description: The CI process executes `npm install -g npm@latest` and updates global binaries, which is a dangerous practice as it modifies the runner environment unexpectedly.
steps_to_exploit: Run the CI pipeline.
The runner environment is modified by a global installation, creating a state that persists for subsequent steps.
kept.impact: Pollution of the build runner environment.

kept.title: Exposure of sensitive GitHub Actions tokens
kept.description: The `npm-publish` workflow uses `id-token: write` and interacts with external registries, which could lead to unauthorized token usage if the workflow is compromised.
steps_to_exploit: Compromise a commit or PR.
Access the `id-token` to authenticate against external services using the repository's identity.
kept.impact: Unauthorized impersonation of the repository in external systems.

kept.title: Inefficient error handling in type checks
kept.description: The `compile` function throws a generic TypeError. Improper handling of this by callers could lead to unhandled promise rejections or process crashes.
steps_to_exploit: Supply an invalid `trust` value to `proxyaddr`.
The function throws a `TypeError` without proper encapsulation.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via unhandled exceptions if the application is not robustly structured.

kept.title: Lack of security focus in dependency updates
kept.description: The Dependabot configuration explicitly ignores major version updates, which are essential for security-critical bug fixes.
steps_to_exploit: A major vulnerability is found in `ipaddr.js`.
Dependabot fails to alert for the update due to the ignore rule.

kept.title: Use of mutable state in trust list generation
kept.description: The `compile` function mutates the `trust` array using `splice.apply`, which is error-prone and can lead to incorrect logic if the input array is modified concurrently.
steps_to_exploit: Pass an array to `compile` that is shared with other parts of the application.
Observe race conditions or logical errors when the array is mutated internally.

kept.title: Potential for ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service)
kept.description: The `DIGIT_REGEXP` is simple, but the lack of input length limits on IP strings could lead to performance issues if large, malformed strings are processed.
steps_to_exploit: Send an exceptionally long string as an IP address.
The parser attempts to process the string, consuming excessive CPU cycles.
kept.impact: Minor DoS risk via CPU exhaustion.

kept.title: Over-privileged CI runner permissions
kept.description: The `scorecard.yml` file uses `security-events: write` and `id-token: write` permissions which may not be necessary if not using specific dashboard features.
steps_to_exploit: Exploit a vulnerability in the `scorecard-action` dependency.
Use the granted write permissions to tamper with repository security metadata.
kept.impact: Increased attack surface for the CI/CD pipeline.

kept.title: Unrestricted usage of unsafe shell execution in build scripts
kept.description: The shell scripts in `ci.yml` utilize `bash -eo pipefail -l {0}`, which can be vulnerable if inputs are improperly sanitized, specifically when constructing paths or dynamic commands.
steps_to_exploit: Manipulate the `matrix` variable in the CI definition.
Inject shell metacharacters into the command execution flow.
kept.impact: Command injection within the build CI runner.

kept.title: Insecure file system cleanup in tests
kept.description: The coverage reporting relies on file patterns that could be manipulated to include files outside of intended paths if a user has write access to the workspace.
steps_to_exploit: Create files with conflicting names in the `coverage` directory.
Observe if the merge script includes unintended files in the final report.
kept.impact: Potential for false coverage results or disclosure of temporary files.
